rationale: Water damage to the policyholder's own basement, flooring, and drywall caused by a burst water supply line inside the home is clearly property damage covered by homeowners insurance.
claim_summary: Sam Patel's basement flooded due to a burst water supply line under an upstairs bathroom sink that leaked for approximately two days while the policyholder was away. Damage includes approximately 2 inches of standing water across the entire basement, buckled hardwood flooring, soaked drywall up to 1 foot, and numerous ruined stored items. High-severity claim requiring immediate professional water remediation and structural assessment.

case_facts.damage_items: hardwood floor buckled, drywall soaked up to 1 foot, stored boxes ruined
case_facts.cause: burst water supply line under upstairs bathroom sink
case_facts.incident_date: while claimant was on work trip; water ran for approximately 2 days

rationale: Wind damage to the policyholder's own roof structure is direct property damage to the home's exterior.
claim_summary: Wind damage claim: four shingles blown off back porch overhang. Estimated repair cost $400 with no water intrusion. Claim falls below the $2,500 deductible and will likely be handled as non-payable, but routed for formal adjuster review and confirmation.

case_facts.description: four shingles blown off roof overhang by wind
